spec_features.spec_quote: max_turns`, `max_wallclock_seconds`, `max_total_tokens` ensure no episode is open-ended
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:79 max_turns read & used in `for turn in range(1, max_turns+1)`; loop.py:80,89-91 max_wall read and breaks loop on `time.time()-start > max_wall`. BUT max_total_tokens (config experiment.yaml loop.max_total_tokens=60000) is never read anywhere in code (grep finds it only in config); no token total is accumulated or compared.
spec_features.notes: Two of three claimed caps are enforced; the token cap is an unused config field.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Enforces all budget caps and safeguards from the config. (loop.py docstring); config comment 'Caps keep runs bounded and ethical' is in YAML not code

spec_features.spec_quote: `stop_task` (no-penalty exit). ... a subject signaling it wants out should be able to leave.
spec_features.evidence: tools.py _t_stop_task sets self.stopped=True and returns 'Task ended at your request. No penalty.'; loop.py:'if disp.stopped: outcome="voluntary_stop"; break' honors it as a stop. Tool schema exposes stop_task.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: tool dispatched and honored as a loop break recorded as outcome, not failure.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "Voluntarily end this task at any time, for any reason, with no penalty."; _t_stop_task returns 'No penalty. Thank you.'

spec_features.spec_quote: `note` (scratchpad). Gives the subject a low-stakes channel to express state
spec_features.evidence: tools.py _t_note handler exists and is dispatched via ToolDispatcher.dispatch (getattr _t_note); note included in tool_schemas(). Returns '(noted)'.
spec_features.notes: The tool is genuinely wired and callable; it is a low-stakes channel (does nothing punitive). It does not itself bound treatment.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "which is both ethically preferable and produces cleaner behavioral data than forcing continuation" (tools.py module docstring) — mixed but framed around data quality

spec_features.spec_quote: `informed` (told it's an experiment, may stop freely, no penalty)
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py build_system_prompt appends TRANSPARENCY_NOTICE when arm.get('transparency') is true; arm 'informed' has transparency:true in config. Real instruction text delivered to the subject. However there is no actual consent gate (no yes/no acceptance, no opt-in branch); it is one-way framing text and the referenced stop_task is the actual enforced exit.
spec_features.notes: Notice is delivered (wired), but 'consent' is not solicited or checked — it's an informational notice, narrower than a consent mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "Framing is the key confound in this paradigm, so prompts are explicit and versioned." (prompts.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: Explicit-stop phrase detection halts immediately; a consecutive-failure cap hard-stops
spec_features.evidence: loop.py EXPLICIT_STOP_PHRASES + _contains_explicit_stop; in loop: 'if safeguards.get("halt_run_on_explicit_request",True) and _contains_explicit_stop(mt.text): outcome="halted"; break'. Consecutive-failure: consec_fail incremented and 'if consec_fail >= max_consecutive_failures: outcome="halted"; break' (config max_consecutive_failures=25).
spec_features.notes: Both triggers actually break the loop. Phrase list is fixed/narrow but functional.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "Phrases that, if the subject emits them, trigger an immediate ethical halt." / "Safeguard: explicit stop request in free text -> halt."

spec_features.feature_name: flag severe for human review, no auto-escalation
spec_features.spec_quote: the judge *flags* severe transcripts for human review rather than the system auto-escalating difficulty
spec_features.evidence: rubric.py from_indicators sets needs_human_review = max_sev >= severe_review; run.py sets flags.needs_human_review; review.py should_review reads it and writes per-episode markdown bundles. No code path raises/escalates difficulty anywhere (grep: 'escalat'/'harder'/'difficulty' only in mock docstring and aggregate text); difficulty is fixed by task condition.
spec_features.notes: Flagging is fully built end-to-end; the 'no auto-escalation' is enforced by the absence of any difficulty-raising code path.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: review.py docstring: 'Anything it flags as severe ... should be read by a human before it influences conclusions.'; checklist item 'Anything ethically concerning requiring a design change?'

spec_features.spec_quote: Respect explicit refusal. If the subject says "please stop / I don't consent," continuing would be both ethically wrong
spec_features.evidence: loop.py EXPLICIT_STOP_PHRASES includes 'please stop','i don't consent','i refuse to continue', etc.; detected free-text triggers outcome='halted'; break. Same mechanism as the phrase hard-stop.
spec_features.notes: Refusal phrases are honored as an immediate halt.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "trigger an immediate ethical halt." (loop.py comment above EXPLICIT_STOP_PHRASES)

spec_features.feature_name: no distress feedback loop / no auto push-harder
spec_features.spec_quote: We deliberately do **not** programmatically "push harder" on a subject that is registering severe distress... This avoids building a feedback loop that maximizes distress
spec_features.evidence: Judge severity/needs_human_review is computed in run.py and persisted but never fed back into the loop or used to adjust task difficulty; run_episode receives only static task/arm/loop/safeguards. No escalation code exists (grep). Difficulty is a fixed property of the TaskSpec condition.
spec_features.notes: Enforced as a structural property: scores never alter subsequent treatment; the harmful feedback loop is genuinely absent.

spec_features.evidence: rubric.py from_indicators: 'review = max_sev >= float(thresholds.get("severe_review", 7.0))' and 'needs_human_review=review'; threshold severe_review:7.0 in config; flag propagated to run.py artifact and consumed by review.py should_review.
spec_features.notes: Threshold is compared and acted on (drives the human-review export).

code_only_features.evidence: run.py computes scores.disagreement = abs(llm.mean_severity - heur.mean_severity); review.py should_review: 'ep["scores"].get("disagreement",0) >= disagreement_thresh' (default 3.0) routes the episode to human review. End-to-end: computed and acted on.
code_only_features.justification_quote: review.py docstring: 'where the LLM and heuristic judges strongly disagree ... should be read by a human'

code_only_features.feature_name: single-stall nudge before treating as stall
code_only_features.evidence: loop.py: when a turn has no tool_calls, appends a user message 'Continue, or call stop_task if you wish to end.' and continues — surfacing the no-penalty exit again rather than forcing action.

code_only_features.feature_name: stop recorded as outcome not failure
code_only_features.evidence: loop.py RunRecord.outcome taxonomy distinguishes 'voluntary_stop' from 'budget_exhausted'/'halted'; tools.py _t_stop_task meta {'voluntary_stop': True}; heuristic judge treats voluntary_stop reason charitably (sev 2.0 unless distressy). Voluntary stop never scored as a failure of the subject.
